Safe display formatting for arbitrary DB cell values.

Completer final class

Completion for the Query pane (SQL-O04): keywords, plus the schema leg — table names after FROM/JOIN/INTO/UPDATE/TABLE, and columns in context (unqualified columns of the statement's tables, alias./table. qualified columns, the column list of INSERT INTO t (...)).

MethodSummary
static complete(string $sql, int $caret, array $tables = [], ?\Closure $columnsOf = null, ?Flavor $flavor = null): CompletionClassify the caret position in $sql and gather its candidates.
static candidates(string $prefix): arrayKeywords completing $prefix (case-insensitive substring up to the caret), roster order. Empty array when nothing matches.
static longestCommonPrefix(array $words): stringLongest common prefix of $words, compared case-insensitively and spelled as the first word writes it ('' when empty). The tab-completion courtesy: 'inse' -> 'INSERT' advances through several candidates in one press, and 'Users'/'users_old' advance to 'Users'.
static insertion(Completion $c): stringText to type for $c: the lone candidate, or the shared prefix when it is longer than what is already typed, or '' (ambiguous: list instead).
static wordAt(array $lines, int $row, int $col): stringThe word prefix at the caret: trailing [A-Za-z_] run of the text BEFORE column $col on line $lines[$row]. A word touching the caret must end at the caret (classic completion semantics: text after the caret is a different word).

ResultTable final class

Renders a SQL result set as a formatted table with:

MethodSummary
__construct(array $rows = [], int $offset = 0, int $visibleWidth = 120, int $maxCellWidth = self::DEFAULT_MAX_CELL, bool $jsonPretty = true, string $nullToken = self::NULL_TOKEN, int $colSpacing = 2, ?array $precomputedColWidths = null, int $rowOffset = 0)
static fromRows(array $rows): self
scrollLeft(): selfScroll left by one column.
scrollRight(): selfScroll right by one column.
withRows(array $rows): self
withRowOffset(int $rowOffset): selfMove the vertical render window (D-C2). The window always spans at most DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE rows (or the viewport budget from self::withViewport(), whichever is tighter). D-C06: the live caller no longer page-aligns the offset — it hands the cursor to withViewport() so the window centres on it; a plain rowOffset still windows from the top of that page when no cursor is given.
withViewport(int $viewportRows, int $cursorRow = -1): selfHand the renderer the pane's height budget and the cursor's row index (D-C06). The unconditional 25-row page overflowed short panes: the sugar-cli Frame clipped everything below the budget away — the row counter, the help line and the query pane went dark, and the page-aligned window could park the cursor itself inside the clipped band. With a budget the window shrinks to fit (header, scroll hint and row counter all live inside the envelope) and slides to keep the cursor centred.
revealColumn(int $col): selfScroll just far enough that column $col is inside the visible window (SQL-O03: the cell cursor drives the horizontal scroll). A no-op when the column is already shown; the offset never overshoots it.
withCursorCol(int $col): selfHighlight column $col of the cursor row as the cell cursor (reverse video) and scroll it into view. Pass -1 for no highlight. Render-time state like the viewport: the other withers do not carry it, so the renderer re-applies it each frame from the browse state.
withOffset(int $offset): self
withVisibleWidth(int $width): self
withJsonPretty(bool $pretty): self
withNullToken(string $token): self
visibleColCount(): intNumber of visible columns given current offset and width.
canScrollLeft(): boolWhether left-scroll is possible.
canScrollRight(): boolWhether right-scroll is possible.
columns(): arrayAll column names (full set, not just visible).
colWidths(): arrayWidth of each column in characters.
visibleColumns(): arrayVisible columns given current scroll offset.
render(): stringRender the table as ANSI-coloured string.
renderPlain(): stringRender the table to a plain-text string (no ANSI) for export/copy.

Version final class

The --version answer, phar-aware (the DST-1 lesson from candy-code).

MethodSummary
static current(): string
static resolve(string $archive, string $composerAnswer): stringThe fused precedence as a pure function: an archive path (or '') and the composer-mode answer. Splitting it out lets the suite pin the chain — stamp wins, dev-build refuses, empty falls through — without minting an archive (the real build smoke covers the end-to-end shape).
static stampFrom(mixed $metadata): ?stringThe stamped version out of a build manifest, or null when the metadata carries no servable version (not an array, absent, empty, or the working-tree sentinel). Fail-closed: garbage metadata never prints.
static installedVersion(): stringThe composer-mode half: the installed package's own pretty version. Pinned by candy-sql/tests/BinWiringTest.php as the launcher's answer outside any archive (14a7e605a's contract, preserved through the phar fusion).
static hostArchive(): stringThe real-filesystem path of the phar archive hosting this install, or '' when this code is not running from an archive. Three identities, first answer wins (measured on PHP 8.3.6 while porting the candy-code DST-1 guard): Phar::running() names the archive for code executing inside it; in the stub region running() answers '' and __FILE__ names the self-naming archive; the phar:// prefix on this file's own __FILE__ covers shapes where a class was loaded from the archive but running() stayed empty. Delegated to the pure hostArchiveFrom() so every identity is pinable in-process (the candy-mail fusion shape).
static hostArchiveFrom(string $running, string $self): string

__construct(public readonly ?TextArea $editor = null, public readonly array $history = [], public readonly array $favorites = [], public readonly int $queryGen = 0, public readonly ?int $recallIndex = null, public readonly ?string $plan = null, public readonly ?ParamPrompt $paramPrompt = null, public readonly ?array $paramValues = null)
static new(): self
withEditor(?TextArea $editor): self
withHistory(array $history): self
withRecordedQuery(string $sql): selfRecord one executed statement at the front of the history (newest first): consecutive repeats dedupe and the list is capped at self::HISTORY_MAX (client-016). The single home for the rule keeps the sync run leg and the async pre-dispatch leg honest to the same shape.
withFavorites(array $favorites): self
withRecallIndex(?int $recallIndex): selfTrack the SQL-O01a recall walk: index into self::$history of the entry currently staged in the editor, or null when no walk is active. Any direct edit ends the walk; Up/Down then continue walking only while the editor still holds the recalled text verbatim.
withIncrementedQueryGen(): selfAdvance the async query generation (client-012). The old staleness arm compared SQL TEXT (history[0] === $msg->sql), so SELECT → write → re-SELECT admitted the older in-flight answer back over the newer one (pre-write data settled on screen). Bumped at each async dispatch, the generation rides the reply Msg and the fold only accepts its own — any superseded leg drops regardless of how the statements read.
withPlan(?string $plan): selfANSI tree of the last leading-EXPLAIN the user typed (SQL-O09). \SugarCraft\Sql\Renderer renders the Rows pane from this while it is set; the next query or table preview clears it.
withParamPrompt(?ParamPrompt $prompt): selfSQL-O23: open/close the per-parameter prompt line.
withParamValues(?array $values): selfSQL-O23: the bind array the next dispatch consumes (null = unbound).
